subject: usul-al-fiqh
summary: Al-Muwafaqat fi Usul al-Shari'ah ('The Reconciliations in the Principles of the Sacred Law') by Imam Ibrahim ibn Musa al-Shatibi (d. c. 790 AH / 1388 CE) is the foundational text of maqasid al-shari'ah (the objectives of Islamic law). It is one of the most original and profound works of Islamic jurisprudence, establishing a systematic theory of the higher purposes of the Shari'ah as the primary framework for legal reasoning.
overview:
Al-Muwafaqat fi Usul al-Shari'ah by the Maliki scholar Ibrahim ibn Musa al-Shatibi (d. c. 790 AH / 1388 CE) is the foundational work in the theory of maqasid al-shari'ah — the higher objectives or purposes of the Sacred Law. Al-Shatibi was a scholar of Andalusian origin who spent most of his career in Granada during the final period of Islamic rule in Spain. His work emerged from deep frustration with what he saw as an over-literalist approach to fiqh that lost sight of the spirit and purposes of the law.

Al-Shatibi systematised the concept of the five essential objectives (al-kulliyyat al-khams) that the Shari'ah is designed to protect: life (al-nafs), intellect (al-aql), lineage or progeny (al-nasl), wealth (al-mal), and religion (al-din). These were not entirely new — earlier jurists had noted them — but al-Shatibi built a comprehensive, theoretically rigorous framework showing how the entire edifice of Islamic law can be understood in terms of its promotion and protection of these objectives.

The book is divided into four sections: (1) The Proofs (al-Adillah) — foundational epistemology of the Shari'ah; (2) The Objectives (al-Maqasid) — the theory of the five necessities, needs (hajiyyat), and improvements (tahsiniyyat); (3) The Legal Rulings (al-Ahkam) — how maqasid inform fiqh; (4) The Mujtahid — the qualifications and methodology of independent legal reasoning.

Al-Shatibi's insistence on the ratio legis (underlying purposes) of rulings, his concept of 'illah (operative cause), and his sophisticated treatment of maslaha (public benefit) within a principled framework made al-Muwafaqat centuries ahead of its time. The work was largely ignored or little-read for centuries after his death, rediscovered and championed by the Moroccan scholar al-Wazzani in the nineteenth century, and subsequently became the cornerstone of the revival of maqasid studies in the twentieth century through the work of Ibn Ashur, Allal al-Fasi, and contemporary Islamic legal theorists.

The standard printed edition is by Dar Ibn Affan (Khobar), edited by Abu Ubaydah Mashhur ibn Hasan Al Salman, in 7 volumes.
structure: Four sections (Adillah, Maqasid, Ahkam, Ijtihad); approximately 7 volumes in the standard edition
